title: Ethical theories, governance models, and strategic frameworks for responsible AI adoption and organizational success
explain_beginner: This paper asks how companies can adopt AI in a responsible way. It looks at moral ideas such as utilitarianism, virtue ethics, and deontology, then asks how those ideas can guide real choices. It also studies who should be answerable, how rules and oversight should work, and how to be open with people. The authors bring these parts together so that doing right and doing well can support each other. For a curious reader, the main point is that adopting AI responsibly is not only a compliance task. It can be part of strategy, helping build trust and create value while considering risk.
explain_business: For executives, this paper argues that AI should be adopted responsibly as a strategic matter, not only a compliance duty. It reviews moral ideas, ways to govern, and plans for putting AI in place. It highlights how governance is organized and what stakeholders do for responsibility and openness, plus methods for judging risks and making decisions. The combined method connects ethics with results and success. In practice, leaders can use it to embed commitments to ethical AI into innovation plans. The decision it informs is how to balance following rules, earning trust, and creating value while adopting AI, so ethical choices become part of how the organization operates and succeeds.
explain_practitioner: The review examines how moral ideas, ways to govern, and planning approaches can guide AI use responsibly in organizations. It connects utilitarianism, virtue ethics, and deontology to practical ways for putting AI into service. It analyzes governance and stakeholder duties for responsibility and openness. The paper then looks at methods for judging strategic risks and making decisions. Its key result is a combined method that ties ethical choices to results. For engineers and researchers, this means ethical work on AI is not separate from deployment. It involves selecting ethical reasoning, assigning ownership, designing open governance, and judging risk so that following rules, earning trust, and creating value are considered together.
